title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
authors: Woosuk Kwon, Zhuohan Li, Siyuan Zhuang, Ying Sheng, Lianmin Zheng, Cody Hao Yu, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Hao Zhang, Ion Stoica
lab: UC Berkeley, with Stanford, UC San Diego and an independent researcher

code.title: vllm-project/vllm
code.note: the authors' serving engine, now a PyTorch Foundation project, Apache-2.0 licence (repo, about 25 minutes for the README and entry path)

takeaway: PagedAttention pages the KV cache into fixed 16-token blocks with OS-style block tables, copy-on-write sharing, and swap/recompute preemption, lifting KV memory utilization from about 20 to 38% to 96% and serving throughput 2 to 4x over Orca; it became the industry-standard KV layout and the foundation of vLLM.
verdict: Believe the mechanism and the memory accounting: the waste figures reproduce from Table 1 and the paper's own length distributions, and paged KV caches became the default of every major serving stack. Treat the throughput multiples as the top of a range: they come from single runs against the authors' own reimplementation of Orca, and read off the paper's figures the gain over the strongest baseline is 1.5 to 2.4x on ShareGPT, about 1.3 to 1.8x on Alpaca, and near 1x where memory is not the bottleneck.

resources.t: vLLM: Easy, Fast, and Cheap LLM Serving with PagedAttention (announcement blog, June 2023)
resources.n: the authors' own short version, with the clearest animations of block tables and copy-on-write sharing, and the up-to-24x-over-Hugging-Face headline.

resources.t: How continuous batching enables 23x throughput in LLM inference
resources.n: the best explanation of iteration-level (continuous) batching, the Orca idea that PagedAttention composes with; benchmarks vLLM against static-batching baselines.

resources.t: Inside vLLM: anatomy of a high-throughput LLM inference system
resources.n: a code-level walkthrough of the modern engine (scheduler, KV cache manager, paged attention kernels), the bridge from this paper to today's codebase.

resources.t: vLLM V1: a major upgrade to vLLM's core architecture (January 2025)
resources.n: what the project learned in a year and a half of production, and how the rebuilt V1 engine changes the scheduler and cache manager described here.

resources.t: vAttention: dynamic memory management for serving LLMs without PagedAttention
resources.by: Prabhu, Nayak, Mohan, Ramjee and Panwar (Microsoft Research India)
resources.n: the strongest critique: it measures what paging costs inside attention kernels and keeps the KV cache contiguous in virtual memory instead.

kb.n: 2017: the KV cache being paged here is the per-token key and value state of its self-attention.

2022: the complementary attention-systems paper; FlashAttention optimises compute and IO inside the kernel, PagedAttention where the KV operands live across requests. Modern engines use both (vLLM V1 integrated FlashAttention 3).
2019: vLLM's distributed execution uses Megatron-style tensor parallelism, with the KV cache manager centralised above it.
2024: multi-head latent attention shrinks the KV cache at the architecture level, the model-side attack on the same bottleneck; vLLM ships FlashMLA kernels for it.
2025: reinforcement-learning post-training generates rollouts with vLLM-class engines (verl, for one, integrates vLLM and SGLang).
2020: the 175B size of the largest model served here, and the source of Figure 10's few-shot translation prefix.
2019: the training-side counterpart, memory as the binding constraint and removed by not storing redundant state.
